marketRegime: Choppy/low-trend 5-minute crypto regime: most observed moves cluster in the 6-20bps range (sub-threshold noise) rather than strong directional momentum, peer-agreement (4/0 'all-agree') is common but not predictive, and price action is mean-reverting enough that momentum entries near 0.55-0.70 ask are only marginally better than a coinflip. The one reliable edge is in outsized moves (20bps+) with ample time remaining (120s+), which occur relatively rarely — explaining why ARB (structural, not momentum-based) outperforms the directional momentum strategy in this regime.

applied.reason: Validated lesson data shows move10-20 bucket is strongly negative (-$33.47, 34.6% win) while move20+ is strongly positive (+$10.14, 56% win). Raising the effective floor to just above the losing bucket (20bps) aligns the filter with the only profitable move-magnitude bucket and should stop admitting weak signals that the current 28bps nominal setting is apparently not fully blocking (recent log shows entries at 6-27bps).

left120+ bucket is the only time-based bucket with positive expectancy (+$10.77, 50.3% win, 175 trades) while left60-120 is validated negative (-$20.25, 35.6% win). Tightening min_entry_left_sec toward 120+ (rather than loosely allowing 148 with decay) reinforces only entering when enough time remains, consistent with the profitable bucket boundary.

Observed live stop exits are firing well below the configured 0.28 (seen at 0.19-0.25), and the left<60s bucket shows catastrophic -1.49 expectancy per trade. Raising the stop threshold tightens risk control and should reduce the size of individual losses that are currently overshooting the intended stop level, likely due to confirm-tick delay combined with fast-moving bid prices.

Reducing confirmation ticks should shorten the lag between stop trigger and execution, addressing the observed gap between configured stop_loss_bid=0.28 and actual fills at 0.19-0.25 which is eroding P&L on losing trades.

Nominal setting of 0.8 is high but live decisions show entries happening at conf=0.57-0.70, well below the stated threshold, suggesting confidence scoring and gating are inconsistent; aligning the threshold with the observed confidence distribution (and down-weighting 'all-agree' which is negative expectancy) should make the filter actually binding rather than cosmetic.

diagnosis: The bot is roughly break-even overall (50.7% win rate, -$68.37 over 404 trades) but the aggregate masks sharply divergent sub-strategies. ARB (92% win, +$5.89 over 13 trades) is strongly profitable but tiny in size/frequency. MOMENTUM, the dominant setup (383 trades, 95% of volume), is the main bleeder at 49% win / -$55.81. Within momentum, the lesson-bucket data is highly informative: 'move10-20' bps moves lose badly (-$33.47 over 81 trades, 34.6% win) and 'left60-120' seconds-remaining entries lose badly (-$20.25, 35.6% win) and 'price<0.45' entries lose (-$19.54, 30.6% win) — these are already correctly vetoed and the recent decision log shows the veto firing repeatedly and correctly skipping move10-20 setups. However the bot is still entering trades with 'left120+' and 'move20+' conditions which are the only genuinely profitable momentum buckets (+$10.77 and +$10.14 respectively), suggesting the edge is concentrated in large momentum moves with lots of time left — current recent ENTERs show moves clustering in the 6-27bps range at ask 0.5-0.65 with ~130-150s left, i.e. borderline/mediocre setups being let through because move>=28bps (momentum_min_move_bps) threshold matches min_entry_left_sec=148 but 'move' values logged (6-27bps) are inconsistent with the 28bps minimum, implying the gating field in logs may differ from the filtre or threshold is not being enforced tightly, or logged 'move' is a different measure than the filtering momentum_move. Per-coin performance is uneven: BTC is the only clearly profitable coin (60% win, +$10.83), DOGE is the worst performer (39% win, -$23.45) and XRP/SOL are also net negative. Exit logic shows take-profit firing frequently near 0.90-0.93 bid and working as intended, but stop-losses are firing at high cost (stop_loss_bid=0.28 but actual stops observed firing at 0.19-0.25, well below the configured 0.28, suggesting stop execution slippage or stop_confirm_ticks delay causing larger-than-expected losses). The 'all-agree' bucket (112 trades, -$18.99, reduce_confidence status) and 'alone' bucket (36 trades, -$4.26, reduce_confidence) indicate peer-agreement signal is not reliable in either direction, undermining confidence calibration tied to peer count. Live diagnostics show 'bad reads: 17948' and 'balance readings unconfirmed', indicating a data-integrity risk that could be corrupting momentum_window inputs. Overall this is a near-coinflip strategy currently being saved by a few well-targeted lesson vetoes, but is not yet net profitable and has mis-tuned risk parameters (stop_loss_bid too tight given it's firing below target, and momentum_min_move_bps too low relative to the profitable move20+ bucket threshold).

Re-score or down-weight the 'all-agree' peer signal in confidence calculation since it correlates with -$18.99 net loss over 112 trades despite being the most frequent context.
